title: Colocation rack power & cooling planning — on-prem GPU pools (Q2 2026)
content:
Purpose:
Plan for next-phase on-prem / colo GPU pool growth: define per-rack power and cooling budgets, physical U-space layouts, PDU/amperage constraints, and rollout checklist for Q2 2026. This is an operational planning sheet — rough numbers and open questions are intentionally included.

Summary / goals:
- Add 48 x A800-equivalent GPUs across two colo sites (site A + site B) to support Dedicated surge capacity and private-customer pools.
- Target average rack PUE and cooling capacity so we don’t exceed facility power draw and can keep inlet temps <= 30C under 95th percentile load.
- Prefer 1:1 cold-aisle containment where feasible; evaluate water-cooled trays if density > 40 GPUs/rack.

High-level assumptions (call these out):
- GPU model used for baseline calculations: NVIDIA Hopper-class A800 (nominal max TDP 350W).
- Typical node: 8x A800 per 2U chassis (8 GPUs per node), with dual PSUs and 3U networking overhead for dense configs.
- Node idle draw: ~120W per GPU-equivalent (includes CPU, NVMe, fans under light load).
- Service overhead per rack: 1 top-of-rack switch (800W), KVM, management 200W.
- Facility power deliverable per rack: negotiable; baseline target is 20kW per rack (208V, 3-phase with 80A PDUs), can push to 30kW with water-cooling/engineering signoff.
- Target operating margin: reserve 15% headroom below facility PDU limit for transient spikes.

Detailed capacity math (baseline):
- Per GPU sustained draw estimate: 300W (conservative for mixed inference workloads).
- For 8 GPUs/node, node draw = 8 * 300W + 200W (CPUs/SSD/fans) = 2,600W ≈ 2.6kW.
- With 42U rack and conservative spacing (account for 3U network + PDUs), we can fit 16 nodes (32U used) => total compute draw = 16 * 2.6kW = 41.6kW (too high for simple air-cooled rack).
- Air-cooled safe configuration (20kW per rack): back-calc nodes supported = floor((20kW - 1.0kW overhead) / 2.6kW) = floor(19kW / 2.6kW) = 7 nodes => 56 GPUs/rack at ~300W/GPU seems inconsistent with earlier density numbers because node size assumption must be rechecked.
- Alternative realistic packing: 4 nodes per rack (2U nodes) would be 8 GPUs/node => 16 GPUs/rack? That’s low density but fits 20kW budget.

Candidate rack profiles (quick variants):
- Profile A — Air-cooled standard (priority: simplicity, lower colo cost)
  - Power budget: 20kW per rack (80A 3-phase); usable ~17kW after 15% headroom.
  - Node config: 2U, 4 nodes/rack (8 GPUs/node) = 32 GPUs/rack.
  - Estimated draw: 32 * 300W + 1.2kW overhead = 10.8kW => comfortably under budget; leaves room for bursty workloads or denser nodes later.
  - Pros: widely supported by colo, cheaper. Cons: lower density, higher rack count.

- Profile B — High-density air + enhanced airflow (containment)
  - Power budget: 24kW per rack (requires colo approval).
  - Node config: 2U, 8 nodes/rack = 64 GPUs/rack (if mechanical layout allows).
  - Estimated draw: 64 * 300W + 1.5kW overhead = 20.7kW => within 24kW.
  - Cons: requires cold-aisle containment and higher fan noise/maintenance; risk if cooling fails.

- Profile C — Liquid-assisted high-density
  - Power budget: 30kW+ per rack, water-cooled rear-door or direct-to-chip allowed.
  - Node config: 4U or specialized trays, 128 GPUs/rack feasible with D2C.
  - Use when we need minimal floor space (e.g., enterprise private racks).
  - Draw: depends on vendor; ensure leak-detection and redundancy.

Site-by-site initial plan (two colo sites):
- Site A (primary): 12 racks available; initial commit: 6 racks. Choose mix: 4 x Profile A, 2 x Profile B to balance density.
  - Compute capacity estimate (approx): (4 * 32) + (2 * 64) = 128 + 128 = 256 GPUs initial.
- Site B (secondary / DR): 8 racks available; initial commit: 4 racks of Profile A for predictable cooling.
  - Capacity: 4 * 32 = 128 GPUs.
- Combined initial on-prem/colo pool: ~384 GPUs across sites. Scaling plan: add 6 racks over 6 months as demand grows.

Power & electrical notes (actionable):
- PDUs: prefer 2x 63A 3-phase PDUs per rack (A+B) on separate feeds. Specify monitoring PDUs with per-outlet metering (Vendor quote VC-3321 covers metered PDUs).
- Breaker requirements: ensure dedicated 3-phase breakers; confirm site wiring (is it 208V vs 400V?) — open question for Site B.
- Generator/UPS: target N+1 UPS for racks serving production Dedicated customers; confirm UPS runtime at expected draw (e.g., 10 racks at 20kW each -> 200kW draw).

Cooling & mechanical notes:
- Baseline air-cooled racks: ensure cold-aisle containment and Aisle-Inlet temp sensors at multiple heights (bottom, mid, top).
- Recommend vendor-supplied airflow management hardware (blanking panels, baffles) for dense racks.
- If any rack > 22kW, require cold-door/water cooling conversation. Obtain quote for Rear Door Heat Exchanger (RDHx) for two candidate racks at Site A.
- Facility PUE target: negotiate for <1.6 at site level for racks consumed by GPU fleet.

Space planning (U count):
- Reserve 3U per rack for networking and management (not counted in GPU capacity).
- Cable management: plan 2U front and rear for cable trays in Profile B/C.
- Weight: approximate 80kg per 2U node (incl rails), ensure floor loading > 1500kg per rack. Confirm with colo.

Network and I/O constraints:
- To avoid top-of-rack bottlenecks, provision 2 x 100GbE uplinks per rack (LACP) and optional 1 x 400Gb spine links later.
- Topology: flat fabric for dedicated clusters; per-tenant VLAN segmentation for private pools.

Cost drivers (rough estimates to include in procurement):
- Colo power premium for >20kW racks: +$2,500 / rack/month vs standard 10kW baseline.
- RDHx retrofit: ~$6k–10k per rack + maintenance.
- Metered PDU (2x63A): ~$2k–3k per rack.
- Installation / commissioning labor: ~16–24 hours per rack.

Open questions / risks (to resolve before ordering):
- Confirm Site B phase/wiring and PDU amperage availability (ticket to colo ops).
- Confirm regulatory/compliance requirements for any customer data in private racks (KMS/HSM proximity).
- Failure modes for RDHx: plan for bypass if water cooling offline — automatic fallback to lower-power mode with GPU shedding policy.
- Spare parts: how many spare nodes and spare PSUs to stock per site? Suggest 2 spare nodes per 12 racks.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- [Sana] Draft vendor RFQ for PDUs and RDHx (ETA 2026-03-08) — link: GH PR above.
- [Ethan] Verify Site B electrical specs with colo rep and upload power diagram (ETA 2026-03-05).
- [Priya] Cost model update for colo tiers and expected monthly burn; incorporate into Dedicated pricing sheet (ETA 2026-03-12).
- [Luca] Run thermal simulation for Profile B racks using baseline workload traces (ETA 2026-03-15).

Appendix: example per-rack quick checklist for install day
- Confirm 3-phase feeds present and separate PDUs installed (A/B).
- Verify rack grounding and bonding.
- Measure floor loading and confirm seismic/anchoring as required.
- Install blanking panels and airflow management hardware before powering nodes.
- Connect and configure metered PDU and integrate with DCIM alerting.
- Run load tests to 95th percentile expected token throughput for 2 hours and confirm inlet temps < 30C.

Notes to self (raw):
- Might need to standardize on a slightly lower-GPU TDP profile (e.g., 260W) for some private customer racks to avoid costly watercooling.
- Check with legal about language for colo contracts referencing liquid-cooling equipment.
- Keep a two-week buffer between receiving racks and provisioning GPUs (cable/PDUs/testing).

End of sheet — comments welcome.
